chapter_theme: After the lion's death the Vidyadhara king resolves to give his daughter to Tivittan, names the eight lords who guard his city, and raises a host of elephants, horses, chariots and foot to escort the bride, as a vimana of gems is conjured at the gate.

cast.role: the bride's father, the Vidyadhara king, named here only by epithets
the red-eyed hero who killed the lion
the spy who brings the news of the lion
the king's kinsmen who take counsel with him
the king's troops, unnamed as a body
men of the host who announce the arrival
the king's younger brother, whose chariot bears the name of blazing fire

one of the eight lords of the Vidyadhara king: lord who guards the Gandharva city, fair of form
one of the eight lords of the Vidyadhara king: lord who guards the fort called Gandhamadhanam, with a golden chariot
one of the eight lords of the Vidyadhara king: king of Chakravalam, named for an elephant-like strength
one of the eight lords of the Vidyadhara king: lord of the Devaravanam, whose chariot outshines the sun's
one of the eight lords of the Vidyadhara king: king of Vijayakoodam, likened to a young elephant lord

827.reading: The poet says that after the red-eyed Tivittan, having beaten the lion, went back to the great city with the moon-bright Vijayan, he will now tell of the father of the maiden destined for him.
827.nuance: Line 2 reads பெர்ந்த where the sense wants பெயர்ந்த; the verse is a hinge that closes the lion episode and opens the wedding section.
827.event: Tivittan, having killed the lion, returns to the city with Vijayan, and the poet turns to the bride's father.

828.reading: A spy brings the king word that the lion has been destroyed, and the king sinks into a sea of joy.
828.nuance: The lion is likened to a young moon coming out of a cave, so the beast's death is praised through the image of its own beauty.
828.event: A spy reports the lion's death to the Vidyadhara king, who rejoices.

829.reading: Thinking the maiden with dark long eyes fit only for the one who killed the lion, the king takes counsel with his kin and begins the wedding rites.
829.nuance: The daughter is given as a reward for the deed; her own wish is not spoken of, only the father's decision with his kin.
829.event: The Vidyadhara king resolves with his kin to give his daughter to Tivittan and begins the wedding preparations.

830.reading: The poet names one of the eight Vidyadhara lords, the lord of the city of Vardhamana, bright-limbed and lotus-eyed.
830.nuance: One of eight verses (830 to 837) that list the lords by city, each praised through his city, chariot or ornament. The name is written in an irregular form here, with a doubled syllable.

831.reading: The poet names one of the eight Vidyadhara lords, the lord who guards the Gandharva city, fair of form.
831.nuance: One of eight verses (830 to 837) that list the lords by city, each praised through his city, chariot or ornament. The name விருகவெல் is not clear and may be corrupt.

832.reading: The poet names one of the eight Vidyadhara lords, the lord who guards the fort called Gandhamadhanam, with a golden chariot.
832.nuance: One of eight verses (830 to 837) that list the lords by city, each praised through his city, chariot or ornament.

833.reading: The poet names one of the eight Vidyadhara lords, the king of Chakravalam, named for an elephant-like strength.
833.nuance: One of eight verses (830 to 837) that list the lords by city, each praised through his city, chariot or ornament.

834.reading: The poet names one of the eight Vidyadhara lords, the lord of the Devaravanam, whose chariot outshines the sun's.
834.nuance: One of eight verses (830 to 837) that list the lords by city, each praised through his city, chariot or ornament.

835.reading: The poet names one of the eight Vidyadhara lords, the king of Vijayakoodam, likened to a young elephant lord.
835.nuance: One of eight verses (830 to 837) that list the lords by city, each praised through his city, chariot or ornament.

836.reading: The poet names one of the eight Vidyadhara lords, the guardian of Kirutha Madhanam, whose name joins Garuda and the golden armlet.
836.nuance: One of eight verses (830 to 837) that list the lords by city, each praised through his city, chariot or ornament. The name is not stated whole; the reading garuda-angadan joins words of the third and fourth lines.

837.reading: The poet names one of the eight Vidyadhara lords, the lord of a city ringed by water and lotus, who bears the earth with his strength.
837.nuance: One of eight verses (830 to 837) that list the lords by city, each praised through his city, chariot or ornament.

838.reading: After posting these eight to guard the city of Rathanupuram, the just king orders a host raised that is like a sea swallowing the whole world.
838.nuance: The host is raised to escort a bride, yet it is pictured as a conquering sea, so a marriage procession borrows the image of war.
838.event: The king leaves eight lords to guard Rathanupuram and orders his army made ready.

839.reading: The troops arrayed elephants like the new moon set in cloud, with ornaments, gear and banners, and burned aloe wood over them.
839.event: The troops deck the war elephants with ornaments, banners and incense.

840.reading: Garlanded warriors gathered, and the horse host rose raising dust from its hooves, the horses bound with ornamented tridents and cloths.
840.event: The warriors gather and the cavalry is made ready and advances.

841.reading: The poet describes the sturdy chariots, with gem-set tops, golden pillars and gem-inlaid floors, mingling in numbers beyond counting.

842.reading: The fighters came round the host, bound in cloth, anklets and garlands, with bright swords, ready for fight.
842.event: The foot soldiers gird themselves and gather around the host.

843.reading: The younger brother of the king, in a chariot named for blazing fire, goes with a sea-like host to guard the bride.
843.nuance: The relation is read from மன்னவற் கிளைய வேந்தன், and the word பேகொண் in line 1 looks corrupt.
843.event: The king's younger brother sets out with his army as the bride's guard.

844.reading: The lord of Aripuram, in a tiger-named golden chariot and kin to the king of the auspicious elephant, arrives with a roaring host.
844.nuance: The word மருமகன் can mean son-in-law or sister's son, so the tie to the king of the auspicious elephant is not fixed.
844.event: The lord of Aripuram arrives with his army.

845.reading: Arkakirti stands on an elephant, with drums sounding and warriors around him, as his sea-like host makes the ground ripple.
845.nuance: The verse leaves unsaid whose son he is; the name is the poem's own.
845.event: Arkakirti stands ready with his army on the field.

846.reading: When the army reached the great gate, men of the host bowed and told it to the king, who created in mind a heavenly vimana shot with rainbow light.
846.nuance: The king is taken to be the Vidyadhara king, since a vimana made by mind is a vidyadhara power, but the verse does not name him.
846.event: Men of the host announce the arrival at the gate; the king raises a vimana by thought.

847.reading: The poet describes the vimana as standing on an emerald stone, shedding green gold light and ending in a blue peak that reaches heaven.

848.reading: The vimana has coral pillars, crystal slabs, gold capitals and strings of pearls and flower garlands hung in its curves.
848.nuance: Line 3 has ஞான்ல, probably a misprint for ஞான்ற, 'hanging'.

849.reading: Gold litters, diamond pillars and garlands hung from every post light the vimana, and all its gems shine in their own colours.

850.reading: Garlands hang from the mouths of carved sea-monsters, gold nets and windows gleam, and banners and tridents shine on the roof.

links.note: Verse 409 reports the sign that within a month Tivittan will split a lion's mouth; verse 828 brings word that the lion has in fact been destroyed.
links.teaches: The prophecy is shown fulfilled by a spy's report, so it reaches the Vidyadhara king as news, not as a vision.

links.note: Kural 381 counts an army first among a king's six limbs, while verse 838 raises the host as a marriage escort, in the likeness of a sea swallowing the world.
links.teaches: The pair shows an army used for display and escort, a use the couplet's list of royal strengths does not name.

gains.a: The verse lacks the couplet's view that an army is a standing limb of rule, not raised for a single occasion.
gains.b: The couplet lacks the case of a host raised for a wedding, where numbers show a king's worth to his allies.

links.note: Kural 676 says to act only after weighing the finish, the hindrance and the yield; verse 829 has the king consult his kin and then press on with the wedding.
links.teaches: A king's deliberation can be a formality over a choice already made by the deed of the suitor.

gains.a: The verse lacks any test of the plan's hindrances, since the lion's death has already decided the match.
gains.b: The couplet lacks a case where counsel follows a settled choice instead of shaping it.

source_issues: 835 line 3: a pulli after a vowel sign was removed by the text repair.
827 line 2: பெர்ந்த looks like a misprint for பெயர்ந்த.
843 line 1: பேகொண் is probably for பேர்கொண்.
848 line 3: ஞான்ல is probably for ஞான்ற.
830, 831, 836: the lords' names are irregular or unclear (பிரீதிதிமா வர்த்த தனன், விருகவெல், கருடன்...அங்கதம்); the cast ids are the nearest readings.
841 line 1 has a stray split in மணித் தொழில்; the sense holds.
